lesson.meaning: To keep something in good condition, or to continue something at the same level.
examples: It's important to maintain good relationships with your colleagues for better teamwork.
We need to maintain a high standard of quality in our products to keep customers happy.
He struggles to maintain a healthy work-life balance with his busy schedule.
Can you maintain a steady pace during the presentation so everyone can follow?
Regular exercise helps you maintain a good fitness level and stay energetic.
lesson.memory_tip: Think of 'maintain' like 'main-tain'ing a car – you keep it working well and in good condition!
